description: A D_PDU split across modem blocks is reassembled; its EOT counts from the block that completed its header, even when its data arrives in a later block. A VDCD busy period in LBT_WAIT holds LBT_WAIT_TIMER like a DCD one.
note: Conn 1 binds SAP 5 for non-ARQ and gets S_BIND_ACCEPTED (A-0041, A-0047); its S_UNIDATA_REQUEST (priority 0 to SAP 5 at 0.0.1.3, U_PDU "hello", no confirmation) is data queued for transmission and produces no SIS output (A-0095, K-0096). Every received D_PDU is a single-segment NON-ARQ-DATA (type 7, address size 4, C_PDU ID as stated, reception window 20) whose segment is a DATA C_PDU holding a DATA S_PDU from SAP 9 to SAP 9 with U_PDU "hi". Burst 1: D_PDU A (0.0.1.3 to 0.0.1.9, C_PDU ID 1, EOT 12) arrives as its first 10 bytes at 2000 and the rest at 3000; its 21-byte header completes at 3000, so its end is 3000 + 6000 = 9000 (C-1024). Burst end 4000: csma.vdcd_end 5000 ms; at 9000 rule 3 gives LBT_WAIT_TIMER 3000 ms. Burst 2 starts at 10000, inside LBT_WAIT: the timer is held (K-0077, K-0087). D_PDU B (C_PDU ID 2, EOT 8) arrives as its header and 5 data bytes at 10500 and the rest at 11000; its header completed at 10500, so its end is 10500 + 4000 = 14500. The burst ends at 11500 with that prediction in the future, so the channel is still busy (K-0073): csma.vdcd_end runs 3000 ms, and at 14500 LBT_WAIT_TIMER restarts with lbt_wait_dcd_ms, 30000 ms (K-0087). Since corpus 0.7.0 the DTS also keeps dts.ttd at the earliest TTD in its transmit queue: started when a request becomes the earliest, cancelled when the transmit queue empties (C-1050).
